name: Democratic Republic of Vietnam
native: Việt Nam Dân chủ Cộng hòa

predecessors.name: French Indochina
predecessors.text: Vietnam north of the 16th parallel, where Chinese Nationalist forces disarmed the Japanese and, after the Ho-Sainteny Agreement of 6 March 1946, French forces replaced them

successors.name: Socialist Republic of Vietnam
successors.text: all of Vietnam: 'officially reunited on 2 July 1976 as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam'

ledger.x: August 1945: the August Revolution page says 'On 20 August, Chiang Kai-shek gave orders for the Chinese First Front Army, under the command of General Lu Han' and that 'General Lu Han's 200,000 Chinese soldiers occupied north Vietnam starting August 1945'; 'The Chinese left only in April-June 1946'.
1945: Hồ Chí Minh declares the independence of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam at Hanoi (2 September).
1946: the Chinese leave (June; the last detachments embark at Haiphong on 15 June).
1946: the First Indochina War begins (19 December, infobox).
1954: the Geneva Accords (21 July; the footnoted agreement is dated 20 July) end the war.
1954: the DRV is confirmed north of the 17th parallel (Geneva Accords, 21 July).
1967: the Ho Chi Minh Trail strip of south-eastern Laos.
1970: the PAVN takes the Cambodian north-east.

1 May 1970: 'elements of SVN PAVN units (28th and 24A regiments) joined with North Vietnamese Army and Pathet Lao to seize Attapeu'; the Ho Chi Minh trail page also has Attapeu and Salavan 'seized by the PAVN during 1970'.
1971: the Pathet Lao and PAVN 'captured the Bolaven Plateau' (Laotian Civil War page, placed in 1971); the Ho Chi Minh trail page has 'During 1971 PAVN took Paksong and advanced to Pakse'.
1972: the PAVN withdraws from the north-east.
1973: the Paris Peace Accords (27 January) leave the PRG and the PAVN in their zones.
1975: the zones merge into the conquest of South Vietnam (30 April, below).

1975: the strip passes to the Pathet Lao state with the end of the Kingdom of Laos: Pathet Lao forces took Vientiane on 23 August 1975 and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed on 2 December 1975.

2 December 1975: the Laotian Civil War 'was officially declared over' and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed, so Attapeu passes to the Pathet Lao state; mirrors kingdom-of-laos /ledger/11.

2 December 1975: the Laotian Civil War 'was officially declared over' and the Lao People's Democratic Republic was proclaimed, so the Bolaven Plateau passes to the Pathet Lao state; mirrors kingdom-of-laos /ledger/12.
1976: North and South unite as the Socialist Republic of Vietnam (2 July); the PRG page: the two 'constitutionally merged to form the current Socialist Republic of Vietnam'.

wars.name: First Indochina War
wars.outcome: Geneva Accords of 21 July 1954: Vietnam 'provisionally divided ... along the 17th parallel'; the DRV holds the north.

wars.name: Vietnam War
wars.outcome: The 1973 Paris Peace Accords (27 January) let the US and its allies withdraw 'By 1973'; the war 'ended on 30 April 1975' with South Vietnam overrun; reunification on 2 July 1976.

certainty.note: Nominal claims and guerrilla fronts: the DRV's real hold is the mountain base and 'most rural areas'; the line north of the 16th parallel was an occupation boundary.
The 17th parallel set by the Geneva Accords, 'provisionally'; the page names no Ben Hai River or DMZ.
The border zones of 1973-1975 were held by the Provisional Revolutionary Government and the PAVN with no agreed lines.

sources.title: Provisional Revolutionary Government of the Republic of South Vietnam
